standard.about: Redlamp is a free raw photo editor for Mac, with Lightroom's layout and shortcuts.
standard.cta: Download it at redlamp.app (link in bio).
standard.requirements: Needs an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26. It's in early development.

episodes.title: Free alternative to Lightroom
episodes.feature: A free, open-source raw photo editor for Mac, with no subscription and no cloud.
episodes.audience: Everyone, and people paying a monthly subscription for photo editing.
episodes.source: README: Support Redlamp (free, no subscription, no cloud); Goals 8 (open source).
episodes.result: A pixel-art dusk, before and after, developed by the four sliders.

episodes.title: Subject mask
episodes.feature: Select the person in one click with an AI mask that runs on the Mac, invert it to select the background, and darken the background so the subject stands out.
episodes.audience: People who edit now and then, portrait and family photographers, people used to phone filter apps.
episodes.source: README: Masking (AI masks: Subject with Apple Vision's built-in models and nothing to download; Invert, as Lightroom's; Subject edges solved per pixel, which brings back stray hairs; mask presets including Darken Background); Models on demand (every model runs on the Mac; photos are never uploaded).
episodes.result: The pixel photo with the background darkened by an inverted Subject mask, before and after.

episodes.title: Film looks
episodes.feature: 36 film looks from 30 real film stocks, built from each film's datasheet.
episodes.audience: People who use film filters and presets, film photographers.
episodes.source: README: Film simulations (36 looks from 30 stocks, built from the manufacturers' datasheets); Lightroom comparison, film stock simulations (Beyond).
episodes.result: The pixel photo in five film looks, one a beat.

episodes.title: Lightroom shortcuts
episodes.feature: Lightroom Classic's keyboard shortcuts, panel order and slider names.
episodes.audience: Lightroom users, especially those who edit from the keyboard.
episodes.source: README: Goals 1; Workspace (Lightroom Classic's keyboard shortcuts, 98 actions on 96 key bindings); Keyboard shortcuts.
episodes.result: The editor's panels in Lightroom's order, then its list of 98 shortcuts, as dashboard panels.

episodes.title: Presets and LUTs
episodes.feature: Lightroom develop presets (.xmp) import with a report of what came across, and .cube and .3dl LUTs import too.
episodes.audience: Lightroom users with presets they made or bought.
episodes.source: README: Workspace, Recipes (.xmp import with a report: exactly, approximately or not at all; .cube, .3dl and HaldCLUT).
episodes.result: The pixel photo with an imported preset, before and after.

episodes.title: Folders
episodes.feature: No import and no catalogue: open a folder and edit. Edits are saved next to each photo and the original is never changed.
episodes.audience: Lightroom Classic users who manage a catalogue, anyone worried about their originals.
episodes.source: README: Why Redlamp (an editor, not a catalog); Workspace, Folders and sidecars; Measured performance (50,000 photos listed in 209 ms).
episodes.result: The Folders panel and the filmstrip full of the folder's photos, as dashboard panels.

episodes.title: Speed
episodes.feature: A slider change renders in 1.8 ms and a 24 MP raw opens in 0.16 s, measured on an M1 Ultra.
episodes.audience: Power users with large shoots, anyone whose editor feels slow.
episodes.source: README: performance card (1.8 ms to render a slider change, 160 ms to open a 24 MP raw, M1 Ultra, Release build); Goals 4. Read again from docs/performance before rendering.
episodes.result: The pixel photo as the Exposure slider moves, a render a beat.

episodes.title: Camera recipes
episodes.feature: Camera-style recipes built from Fujifilm-style recipe cards: hover to preview one on your photo, click to apply it, then set its amount.
episodes.audience: Fujifilm shooters and people who follow film recipes.
episodes.source: README: Workspace, Recipes (39 bundled recipes, including camera-style ones built from Fujifilm-style recipe cards; hover to preview, click to apply, adjust the Amount); Screenshots (Chrome Street on a Fujifilm X-T3 RAF); Lightroom comparison, camera recipe cards (Lightroom: No). The card editor itself is only in the Recipe Lab, so the video doesn't show typing a card.
episodes.result: The Chrome Street recipe on the pixel photo, before and after.

episodes.title: Remove by name
episodes.feature: Type the name of what to remove, such as power lines, and Redlamp finds and removes it, on the Mac with no credits.
episodes.audience: Occasional editors, travel and street photographers.
episodes.source: Lightroom comparison, find and remove things named in words (Done, RM-08); README: In progress, Remove (Find, Remove All); Goals 6 (no cloud and no credits). Check the README's status before building.
episodes.result: The pixel street before and after its power lines are removed.

episodes.title: Focus stacking
episodes.feature: Redlamp finds focus stacks for you and merges them into one sharp photo that edits like a raw.
episodes.source: README: Goals 6 (Lightroom doesn't offer focus stacking); Focus stacking (stacks are found for you, the result develops like a raw).
episodes.result: A merged focus stack against one of its frames, in pixel art.

posts.caption:
A free raw photo editor for Mac, with no subscription and no cloud. Redlamp is open source, and it has Lightroom's layout and shortcuts. Download it at redlamp.app (link in bio). Needs an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26. It's in early development. Redlamp isn't affiliated with Adobe.

#photoediting #rawphoto #lightroom #macos #photography
posts.alt: Pixel art of Redlamp's lamp lighting up in the dark and becoming its logo, with the title Free alternative to Lightroom. Then a colourful photo editor with a pixel-art dusk: four coloured sliders brighten it and bring out its colour over a live histogram, as the words No subscription, No cloud and Open source appear one after another, each with a card: $0 per month, nothing uploaded, and the MPL-2.0 licence. The backslash key shows the dusk before and after, then it fills the frame, before and after the edit. The video ends with Download free, redlamp.app.
